notes.text: David Jiříček has started playing on the power play: on the ice for 41% of the team’s power-play time in 10 games, up from 2% last season.
Chris Kreider is out (lower body injury) and has missed the last 4 games.
Josh Anderson is out about 3-4 weeks (lower body injury) and has missed the last 3 games.

Mike Matheson is out about 3-4 weeks (lower body injury) and has missed the last 4 games. He is a top-four defenseman. Alexandre Carrier has taken his spot beside Kaiden Guhle. That pair has had 38% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 33:41 together, down from 54% with Matheson.
Brett Berard was added to the roster on Nov 16 and has played beside Oliver Kapanen and Owen Beck.
Oliver Kapanen is no longer killing penalties: 1% of the team’s shorthanded time in 16 games, down from 33% last season.
Arber Xhekaj has started killing penalties: on the ice for 29% of the team’s shorthanded time in 22 games, up from 6% last season.

story.head: Expect the Canadiens to fire from everywhere
paras: Both teams have won two in a row. Going in, the Flyers are fifth in the Metropolitan (tied for 20th in the NHL) and the Canadiens second in the Atlantic (tied for fourth).
The Flyers’ record (.440) is about what their chances are worth. The Canadiens’ record (.696) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.548), largely because they’re 9-5 in one-goal games.

The Flyers play slow, tight games (2nd lowest), take away shots from the point (3rd lowest) and get a lot of their shots blocked (29th). Philadelphia has scored 2.52 goals a game, the fourth fewest in the league. As for the Canadiens, they get into more chippy games than almost anyone (2nd) and have had some of the best goaltending in the league (4th), but take more penalties than they draw (31st). The Canadiens are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Flyers. On top of that, the Habs’ defensemen shoot a lot, and the Flyers’ not so much.

Matvei Michkov (11 G / 8 A / 19 P in 25 GP) leads the Flyers in scoring, and Trevor Zegras (5 G / 10 A / 15 P in 25 GP) isn’t far behind. For the Canadiens, Lane Hutson (5 G / 19 A / 24 P in 23 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Cole Caufield (12 G / 8 A / 20 P in 23 GP) has a team-high twelve goals.
Dan Vladař (3-5-4 / .874 SV% in 12 GS) is expected to go for Philadelphia. Jacob Fowler (10-2-2 / .924 SV% in 14 GS) has been outstanding for Montréal and is expected to start.

items.text: The Canadiens are newly without Josh Anderson, and have been without Chris Kreider, Samuel Montembeault and Mike Matheson for several games. Jacob Fowler is expected to start.
Travis Konecny has a point in five straight games against Montréal.
Juraj Slafkovský has two goals on chances worth about 8.2 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.
Trevor Zegras is two goals from 100.
